history.content: Why was the mountain in Gales Crater named Mount Sharp?
The mountain in Gale Crater was informally named "Mount Sharp" to pay tribute to geologist Robert P. Sharp.
Is there or was there a life in the past?

I cannot provide specific information to confirm or deny the existence of life on Mars, either in the past or present. However, it has many signs that water was present over its history which is a key ingredient of life.   That's why our search for evidence of life on Mars focuses on areas where liquid water was once stable.  Chemical and geothermal energy, for example, are also energy sources for life forms on Earth. Perhaps tiny, subsurface microbes on Mars could use such energy sources, too.
I have noinformation on Dr. Robert P. Sharp.
How do you measure height and depth of the mountain from afar?

The height and depth of a mountain like Mount Sharp can be measured from afar using remote sensing techniques. One common method is LIDAR (Light Detection and Ranging), which uses light, in the form of a pulsed laser, to measure variable distances to the Earth or other planetary bodies. By combining these light pulses with other data, scientists can obtain precise, three-dimensional information about the shape and surface characteristics of the mountain, including its height and depth.

NASA technology has numerous applications in our daily lives. These technologies, known as NASA spinoffs, often become solutions to challenges that were not initially intended to be solved. We’ve profiled more than 2,000 spinoffs since 1976 — there’s more space in your life than you think! For example, memory foam, scratch-resistant lenses, and artificial limbs are all spinoffs that have benefited life on Earth. Other NASA technologies include GPS and have improved communication and weather forecasting. NASA helps find where the wildfires are and PPE for firefighters include a fire helmet; fire-resistant pants, jackets and gloves; and steel-toed, waterproof boots.
I want to visit NASA!  How can I get there?

There are several ways to visit NASA, depending on which center or facility you would like to see. Here are a few options: Johnson Space Center in Houston, Texas: Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland: Kennedy Space Center in Florida.  Also, you may be interested to visit:
1. **NASA Socials**: These are unique opportunities for NASA's social media followers to learn and share information about NASA's missions, people, and programs. You can find out more about NASA Socials [here](https://www.nasa.gov/connect/social/index.html).
2. **Live Launches**: Witnessing a live rocket launch is a jaw-dropping, bucket-list experience. Visitor Centers at Kennedy Space Center and Wallops Flight Facility provide the closest public viewing of rocket launches with live launch commentary from space experts. You can learn more about Live Launches [here](https://www.nasa.gov/connect/visitor/index.html).
I recommend checking their official website for more information on tours, events, and visitor policies.

The situation will vary, depending on the nature of the event. It is best to take immediate protective action as soon as you think there is a local emergency, or if you hear on the radio or television that you need to shelter-in-place.
